## What
Write bash tests that verify the structural boundaries of the documentation changes introduced by this story, per the behavioral testing standard Rule 5 (instruction files — test the structural boundary, not the content).

Tests to write in tests/skills/test-inference-review-docs.sh:

1. CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md contains a section heading for preconditions.inference_review.rate_rationale
2. CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md contains a section heading for preconditions.inference_review.rate_high_stakes  
3. preplanning SKILL.md Phase E dispatch block contains 'mode:' as a task argument
4. CLAUDE.md contains 'META_QUESTION' (new signal documented)
5. CLAUDE.md contains both META_QUESTION and REPLAN_ESCALATE (distinction documented, neither removed)

Each test should grep the file for the structural marker and assert its presence. Do NOT test content/wording — only that the structural element exists.

Follow the existing test file pattern in tests/skills/ (shebang, set -euo pipefail, REPO_ROOT setup, pass/fail counters).

Make the file executable: chmod +x tests/skills/test-inference-review-docs.sh

Satisfies: behavioral testing standard structural boundary requirement for documentation changes.
